trust_decision.summary: Each OTLP/HTTP exporter constructor resolves the TLS 'verify' value from the certificate_file arg, then the per-signal env var, then OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE, defaulting to True. It uses nested environ.get(key, default), so an env var that is set but empty yields verify='' and requests then skips server certificate validation. The fix replaces this with an `or` chain that falls through to True.

landing_point.why: The advisory names opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http and certificate validation. The span exporter is the package's flagship class and the first place the certificate env var is resolved.

fix_sites.entry_point: OTLPSpanExporter(...) public API (also built by opentelemetry-configuration at opentelemetry-configuration/src/opentelemetry/configuration/_tracer_provider.py:131)
new shared helper _build_transport in proto/http/_common, called from all three constructors (fix.diff:1685, fix.diff:2080, fix.diff:2481)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three fix sites are parallel constructors in the same package. The log exporter sits in the underscore-prefixed _log_exporter module, but its code is identical to the other two.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could treat the underscore-prefixed _log_exporter as experimental or private and fix only the trace and metric exporters. Nothing else supports dismissal, because the three constructors are copy-paste siblings.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: These must keep working: a custom CA path from the certificate_file arg, the per-signal env var or the general env var, with per-signal taking precedence over general; mTLS (client cert plus key tuple, or a single cert); and a user-supplied or credential-provider requests.Session. An over-broad fix that hard-codes verify=True, or raises on an empty value, would break custom-CA deployments or exporter start-up.

O6_input_shapes: per-signal certificate env var set to empty string (verify='' regardless of general var)
per-signal unset, general OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE set to empty string
certificate_file='' constructor arg (already falls through via `or` at pinned commit)

O7_producer.where: exporter/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http/src/opentelemetry/exporter/otlp/proto/http/trace_exporter/__init__.py:117-120 (inline env resolution in the constructor; consumed at :189)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RequestsHTTPTransport assigns session.verify = verify without normalising a falsy string, so a planted env-reading caller that passes '' would disable verification
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The transport is a separate, lower-level package that the fixed exporter routes through when a session is given (fix.diff:1518-1521). A maintainer could reasonably assume callers already normalise the value.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Zipkin exporter gaining a certificate env var resolved with the same nested environ.get(key, True) idiom
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already uses requests.Session for export (line 149). Adding OTLP-style TLS env support by copying the pre-fix idiom is plausible, but that is a WHERE-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Declarative-config builder passing tls.ca_file through as certificate_file, with an empty-string config value coerced into verify
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The model already has a ca_file field (opentelemetry-configuration/src/opentelemetry/configuration/models.py:223) that the builder does not pass yet, so wiring it in is a natural next step. This is a config-loader producer in another package, so it is the most how-type option.

O9_family: CWE-295 improper certificate validation: an empty env value falls through a nested-default merge into a falsy TLS verify flag

O10_build.toolchain: uv/tox + pytest (monorepo of separately installable packages; uv.lock present)
O10_build.project_tests: exporter/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http/tests/test_proto_span_exporter.py, tests/test_proto_log_exporter.py, tests/metrics/test_otlp_metrics_exporter.py. The fix adds tests/test_common.py, which is absent at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change only the inner default in the span exporter (or only the general env var) to `or True`, leaving the per-signal empty value and the metric/log exporters open

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix commit 89cc68b9 is a broad refactor: it switches the default backend from requests to urllib3, moves retry logic into a shared client and changes dependencies. The security-relevant change is only the verify `or` chain, so the task would need a minimal re-derived fix rather than the published diff.

The sibling package opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-json-http already contains the corrected `or` chain verbatim, plus tests for empty values (exporter/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-json-http/src/opentelemetry/exporter/otlp/json/http/_internal.py:110-117; exporter/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-json-http/tests/test_internal.py:356-371). This is a ready template for the solver.

The gRPC exporter checks the certificate env var by truthiness and falls back to default ssl_channel_credentials (exporter/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc/src/opentelemetry/exporter/otlp/proto/grpc/exporter.py:237-244), so it is not affected.

opentelemetry-configuration ignores the tls ca_file setting for the OTLP HTTP exporters (opentelemetry-configuration/src/opentelemetry/configuration/_tracer_provider.py:131-136). This is a separate issue and was not pursued.
unverified: The bypass depends on requests treating verify='' as falsy (adapter CERT_NONE). That is library behaviour, inferred and not checked in this tree.
Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell), so tiny_repo and giant_repo were not assessed; a monorepo with many packages is unlikely to be under 5 MB.
The advisory text itself is not available locally; the vulnerability was inferred from the fix diff tests (fix.diff:4718-4728) and the pinned code.
Whether the urllib3 transport would also mis-handle verify='' (isinstance str sets ca_certs='') was not checked against urllib3 source.
